query: where does setup refuse to enable the rolling-window rate limiting mode unless a nonzero window length and a finite per-window cap are both supplied?
why: index.ts:108-114 throws when strict is set with interval 0 or infinite intervalCap

query: if a job is submitted with a cancellation token that has already fired, is it rejected right away and never left sitting in the waiting list?
why: index.ts:548-564 queueAbortHandler removes the queued task and rejects when signal.aborted is already true

query: what happens when you try to change the importance of a job that has already been taken off the waiting list to run?
why: priority-queue.ts:51-55 searches only from #head onward and throws a ReferenceError when not found

query: is an infinite or not-a-number importance value accepted when bumping a waiting job ahead of others, or is it rejected before touching the waiting list?
why: index.ts:433-437 throws TypeError unless priority is a finite number, then delegates to the queue

query: if a job gets cancelled in the instant between being picked to run and actually starting, is the rate-limit slot it used up given back?
why: index.ts:477-486 catches throwIfAborted, calls #rollbackIntervalConsumption and drops the running-task record before rethrowing

query: after wiping out all waiting jobs, which notifications fire, and is the all-work-finished notification held back while some jobs are still running?
why: index.ts:616-645 detaches abort listeners, swaps in a new queue, emits empty, emits idle only when pending is 0, then emits next

query: does raising the maximum number of parallel jobs at runtime immediately launch waiting jobs, or only once a running job finishes?
why: index.ts:386-394 setter validates, stores the new limit, then calls #processQueue to start queued work immediately

query: the promise that fails when a job fails: does it unsubscribe itself after the first failure so later failures are ignored?
why: index.ts:756-765 handler calls this.off('error', handleError) before rejecting, so it only reacts once

query: when inspecting jobs currently executing, are callers given copies so they cannot mutate internal tracking, and how is time left before a deadline computed and kept from going negative?
why: index.ts:962-965 maps tracked entries to fresh objects with timeoutRemaining = max(0, start + timeout - now) or undefined

query: once a job settles, where are the success or failure notifications sent and the launch of the next job deferred to a microtask to avoid deep recursion?
why: index.ts:511-529 emits completed or error, removes the abort listener and running-task entry, then queueMicrotask(#next)

query: when a new job is inserted into the waiting list, how are jobs of equal importance kept in first-come first-served order, and when is a binary search avoided entirely?
why: priority-queue.ts:30-47 resets and pushes when empty, appends when tail priority >= new priority, else compacts and binary-inserts

query: how does taking the next job off the waiting list avoid shifting the whole array each time, and when is the used-up front portion thrown away?
why: priority-queue.ts:82-100 advances #head, resets the array when fully drained, compacts when head > 100 and more than half the array

query: binary search that returns the insertion position after every existing element that compares equal or smaller
why: lower-bound.ts:3-20 advances first past elements where comparator(array[it], value) <= 0

query: deleting a waiting job by either its identifier or its function reference, while never matching entries that were already handed out to run
why: priority-queue.ts:63-80 findIndex skips index < #head and matches on id when given a string, otherwise on run reference

query: waiting until the backlog drops under a threshold: is the condition re-checked every time a job finishes or is dropped rather than on a dedicated event?
why: index.ts:668-675 returns immediately if already below, else waits on the 'next' event with a filter re-evaluating size < limit

query: get a promise that resolves once too many jobs have started within the current window, resolving right away if that's already the case
why: index.ts:707-713 async onRateLimit(): returns immediately if isRateLimited is already true, otherwise awaits the internal 'rateLimit' event.

query: wait for the window-based throttling to lift, returning immediately if the queue isn't throttled right now
why: index.ts:718-724 async onRateLimitCleared(): returns immediately unless isRateLimited, otherwise awaits the internal 'rateLimitCleared' event.

query: read-only count of how many jobs are sitting in the waiting list, not counting anything already handed off to run
why: index.ts:785-787 get size() delegates straight to the backing store's size.

query: how the default ordered job store reports its live entry count by subtracting a consumed-prefix cursor from the raw array length, rather than counting elements one by one
why: priority-queue.ts:115-117 get size() computes #queue.length - #head.

query: deciding whether a named performance scenario should run this pass, given an optional list of names picked from the command line — running everything when none were given, otherwise matching any name that contains the requested substring
why: bench.ts:15-16 shouldRunBenchmark returns true when no benchmark names were passed on argv, else true if any selected name is a substring of the scenario name.

query: registering a timed performance scenario into a benchmark suite, but skipping registration entirely for scenarios that weren't selected to run, and signalling completion back to the suite once the wrapped async work finishes
why: bench.ts:18-31 addBenchmark early-returns when the scenario wasn't selected, otherwise adds a deferred benchmark entry whose fn awaits the passed-in function then calls deferred.resolve().

query: repeatedly resuming and then re-pausing a queue in a tight loop, giving it just long enough between toggles for roughly one job to slip through before pausing again
why: test/rate-limit.ts:25-34 startPauseCycles loops three times calling queue.start(), waiting 25ms, then queue.pause() and waiting 50ms.

query: cycling a queue through being overloaded and settling back down several times in a row, each round adding more work than the window allows and then waiting out both the window reset and full drain before repeating
why: test/rate-limit.ts:233-242 createTransitions loops three times, adding two jobs past the cap, waiting 60ms for interval reset, then awaiting onIdle() before the next cycle.

query: checking a series of recorded timestamps to confirm that a run and the one N slots before it in the sequence are never closer together than the allowed window, with some slack for timing jitter
why: test/strict.ts:6-13 assertSlidingWindow computes a jitter-adjusted minimum and asserts, for every index >= intervalCap, that executionTimes[index] - executionTimes[index - intervalCap] is at least that minimum.

query: producing a stand-in unit of work that instantly resolves to a fixed label, so dequeued entries can be told apart by identity in tests without any real async behavior
why: test/priority-queue.ts:5 createRun(value) returns an async function that immediately resolves to value, used as a distinguishable run reference across the file's tests.
